info.title: Crokinole tournament API
info.summary: Read the draw, score a match, and pull the season ranking.
info.description:
The tournament runs on a laptop in the hall. Everything here is served by that laptop over the venue's own network, so the API is reachable from any phone, tablet or scoring machine on the same wifi and from nowhere else.

## Two ways to call

Every call is one action. Both of these are the same request:

    GET  /api/state
    GET  /api.php?action=state

The path form is the one to use. The query form is older and still works, so nothing that already integrates has to change.

Anything that changes something takes POST with a JSON body; reads take GET. Responses are always JSON with an `ok` field, and a failure carries `ok: false` and a human-readable `error`.

## Scoring

A match is four sets. Each set is won by whoever scored more **in that set** and is worth 2, or 1 each when the set is level, so a match shares out 8 points. Points scored inside a set decide that set and nothing else: a team can score far more across the four sets and still lose the match.

Send the per-set breakdown and the laptop works the match points out itself. `points_a` and `points_b` in a response are always match points, out of 8.

## Who may call what

- **Reading the draw and the ranking** needs nothing.
- **A scoring machine** sends an `X-Api-Key` header. The key is generated per event and shown in the organiser screen.
- **A player** proves they belong to the match with a code: the match code from the board, their team code, or the event's play code.
- **The organiser** sends the event's PIN.

Every result records who entered it, so a score is always traceable back to a phone, the machine, or the organiser.

get.description:
Everything the board needs in one call: the event, its poules, the standings per poule, and every match in the current round. Poll this rather than holding a connection open.

Standings are keyed by poule id. The key `0` holds teams not yet placed in a poule.

200.description: The current state. `event` is null when no tournament has been created yet.

running.summary: A tournament in its third round

get.description:
The whole draw rather than just the current round, grouped by round number. The board uses this to draw the knockout bracket.

Note that `sets_a` and `sets_b` carry match points out of 8, not a count of sets; the name is older than the rule.

post.description:
Change what the projector is showing, from somewhere else in the hall.

Written for a control surface at the jury desk: one button puts the knockout up when the final starts, another goes back to the poules. Bitfocus Companion can do this with its built-in HTTP module and no custom code.

A command is obeyed **once**. The board then goes back to running itself, rather than being frozen on whatever was last pressed. Each command carries a sequence number the board remembers, so reloading the page does not replay an old instruction and a button pressed twice does the obvious thing.

Naming a view stops the automatic cycling, since choosing a screen is a deliberate act. Send `autocycle: true` with it to pick a view and keep cycling anyway.

Takes either credential: the API key, which is scoped to this one tournament and is the better choice for a control surface, or the organiser PIN.

schema.description: Send at least one of view, poule_page or autocycle.

view.description: Which screen to show: the poule tables, the knockout bracket, or what is on each table.

poule_page.description: Jump to a page of poules, counting from 1. The board shows four at a time.

autocycle.description: Whether the board keeps moving between views on its own.

knockout.summary: Put the knockout up for the final

resume.summary: Back to the poules, cycling again

freeze.summary: Stop cycling and stay where it is

page.summary: Show a particular page of poules

200.description: Passed on. The board picks it up within a couple of seconds.

400.description: Nothing to do, or a view that does not exist.

example.error: view must be poule, ko or tables.
Send the API key or the organiser PIN.

get.summary: What is on each table right now
get.description:
Call this first, once per round. It tells a machine which match is at which table, so a camera pointed at table 4 knows what it is watching.

`table` is the table in the hall, counted straight through, one match per round. One camera covering several tables can map each of its tables to a match from this one call, then score each by number. The draw changes every round, so call it again each round.

Every match also carries a `match_code`, which never changes and is never ambiguous.

parameters.name: round
parameters.description: Which round to list. Defaults to the round being played.

post.description:
Record a score for one match.

## Saying which match

One of three, in order of preference:

1. `match_code` — from the board or from ingest_tables. Never ambiguous.
2. `match_id` — the numeric id from ingest_tables.
3. `table` — the table in the hall, plus `round`.

`table` means the physical table, counted straight through the hall, which is one match per round. A camera above table 7 can send `table: 7` and does not have to know which poule happens to be sitting there. Take the numbers from ingest_tables at the start of each round: they are redrawn every round, because who plays where changes.

Do not confuse it with `poule_table`, the number on the players’ own schedule, which counts within a poule and so repeats once per poule.

If a number somehow still matches more than one match it is refused with a 409 rather than guessed at. Sending the wrong result to the wrong table is far worse than an error.

## Sending the score

Send `sets`: an entry per set with points and 20's for both teams. The laptop works out the match points, so a bug in a client cannot invent a scoreline. `pa` or `pb` may be null for a set not yet played.

Set `complete: true` only when all four sets are in. Until then the result is held as in-progress and does not count toward the standings, which lets a machine stream a match as it happens without a half-finished score reaching the table.

Sending the same result twice is harmless: it overwrites with the same values.

200.description: Recorded. The match is returned as it now stands, so the caller can check what was stored rather than assume.

example.error: Table 4 is ambiguous in round 3 (2 matches). Send match_code, or add "poule".

post.summary: Enter a score from a phone
post.description:
The same path a machine uses, with a different proof of identity. `code` may be the match's own code, the team code of a team playing in it, the event play code, or the organiser PIN.

Save freely as the match goes on with `complete: false`; the phone does this on every keystroke. The result only counts once `complete` is true.

A result the organiser has confirmed is locked, and a player sending to it gets a 409. The organiser can still change it.

403.description: The code does not open this match.

example.error: Not your match, or wrong code.

404.description: No such match in this event.

409.description: The organiser has confirmed this result and it is locked.

get.description: Field-Weighted Points across the season, and the nights that count toward it. Public, so croki.nl can render it in its own design.

parameters.name: season
parameters.description: Which season. Defaults to the current one.

post.description: The event with its codes and the machine API key, all teams with their login codes, and every match. Guarded by the PIN because it hands out the codes that let people score.
The number of rounds is the poule stage; the knockout is drawn separately once the poules finish.

admin_pin.description: Set now; needed for every organiser call afterwards.

play_code.description: Optional shared code that lets any player enter any score.

advance_per_poule.description: How many teams go through from each poule.

player2.description: Leave out for a singles tournament.

200.description: Added, with the login code the team will use.

post.description: For pasting an entry list in rather than typing 44 teams one at a time.
Pairs each poule for the round, avoiding rematches where it can and giving an odd team out a bye. A bye counts as a clean sweep, all four sets.

round.description: Which round to draw. Defaults to the next one.

post.description: Takes the qualifiers from every poule, plus the best runners-up needed to fill the bracket, and seeds them so that poule winners meet as late as possible.

size.description: Bracket size, a power of two.

bronze.description: Whether to play a third-place match.

post.description: Normally unnecessary: winners are carried through automatically as results come in. This forces it.
The organiser's override. Set `status` to `confirmed` to lock a result so a phone cannot change it afterwards.

points_a.description: Match points out of 8. Prefer sending sets and letting them be worked out.

post.description: Wipes every score and draw but keeps the teams. There is no undo.

MachineKey.name: X-Api-Key
MachineKey.description: Generated once per event and shown in the organiser screen. It is scoped to that one event, so a leaked key cannot touch another tournament. May also be sent as `api_key` in the body.

AdminPin.name: admin_pin
AdminPin.description: The organiser PIN, sent as `admin_pin` in the request body.

EventId.name: event_id
EventId.description: Which tournament. Defaults to the one running, so this is rarely needed.

Error.description: Every failure looks like this. The message is meant to be readable by a person.

MatchStatus.description: pending: drawn, nothing entered. progress: partly entered and auto-saved, does not count. entered: complete, counts. confirmed: the organiser has locked it.

SetScore.description: One set. Points decide who wins the set; 20's are recorded but never decide it.

pa.description: Points team A scored in this set. Null if the set has not been played.

pb.description: Points team B scored in this set.

ta.description: 20's by team A in this set.

tb.description: 20's by team B in this set.

current_round.description: Higher than num_rounds once the knockout has started.

StandingRow.description: One row of a poule table. Ordered by points, then 20's; a tie for first is broken by the head-to-head result between the teams level at the top.

points.description: Match points: 2 per set won, 1 per level set, so up to 8 per match.

table_no.description: The number on the players’ schedule, within their poule.

phys_table.description: The table in the hall. Null for a bye.

team_b.description: Null when the match is a bye.

points_a.description: Match points out of 8, not points scored.

match_code.description: Shown on the board. Four characters, no I, L, O, 0 or 1 so it cannot be misread.

shootout_winner.description: Team id, when a level knockout match went to a shoot-out.

scored.description: Whether this counts toward the standings yet.

MatchPublic.description: A match as returned to a phone or a scoring machine.

table_no.description: The number on the players’ schedule, within their poule.

phys_table.description: The table in the hall. Null for a bye.

table.description: The table in the hall. This is the one to score against. Null for a bye, which is played at no table.

poule_table.description: The number on the players’ schedule, counted within the poule, so it repeats once per poule. Not usable on its own to identify a match.

standings.description: Keyed by poule id, as a string. Key "0" holds teams not yet in a poule.

board.description: What the big screen was last told to do from the jury desk. The board obeys a sequence number it has not seen before, once.

server_time.description: Unix seconds, for spotting a clock that has drifted.

IngestScoreRequest.description: Identify the match with exactly one of match_code, match_id, or table.

table.description: The table in the hall, as returned by ingest_tables. One match per round. Send `round` with it.

poule.description: Only needed to disambiguate a per-poule table number on a draw made before tables were numbered through the hall.

sets.description: Up to four sets. The laptop works the match points out from these.

shootout_winner.description: Team id, for a level knockout match.

complete.description: True only when all four sets are in. Until then the result does not count.

source.description: Recorded against the result so it can be traced back.

code.description: The match code, a team code of a team in the match, the event play code, or the organiser PIN.
